opening_message:
Ticket 1: Kathryn Bishop (employee ID E023) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E023.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Kathryn Bishop (E023) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; write is at the maximum for this role, so recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E023 is a contractor with basic training. Contractors with basic training max out at read; requested write exceeds this, so recommend read.
reason: The two notes about E023 conflict on employment type: the first (HR) says full-time, while the security note says contractor with basic training. Under the security record, a contractor with basic training has a maximum of read, and the requested write exceeds that. Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the most restrictive permitted level, read.
